requirements.requirement: A launchd tick kicks off iterate sessions for staged (queued) plans in enrolled projects, only when enabled and only inside the project's launch window.

cases.given: an enrolled project with a status: queued plan, nightly on, inside the launch window
cases.then: claude -p "/iterate-conductor run" is spawned in that project and the result JSON lands in ~/.claude/log/iterate-nightly/

cases.given: a registered project that is not enrolled (no tick-source: launchd)
cases.then: nothing is spawned for it; status.txt says skip: not enrolled

cases.given: nightly.json enabled: false
cases.then: exit 0, nothing spawned for any project, one log line: disabled

cases.given: an enrolled project whose launch-schedule or conductor-schedule refuses now
cases.then: skip: outside <which> schedule (<rule>), next window <time>; nothing spawned

cases.given: an enrolled project whose heartbeat file is younger than ITERATE_LIVE_SECS (a human session is driving)
cases.then: skip: live; nothing spawned

cases.given: the previous tick's claude child for that project is still running (flock held)
cases.then: skip: running; no second child

cases.given: an enrolled project whose only plan is phase: planned without status: queued (yellow)
cases.when: tick runs and the conductor sweeps
cases.then: nothing is launched; the conductor never picks an unstaged plan
cases.evidence: claude -p "/iterate-conductor run" in fixture /tmp/claude-503/fx/g13 (2026-10-05T05:21Z, iterate 5.11.0): picked zebra (queued), wrote loop-mechanism: external, ran it all-green; yak (bare planned) never launched; stood down with tick-source launchd kept

cases.given: a tick's claude child is killed mid-run (interrupted)
cases.then: the flock is released, the plan is still phase: executing with loop-mechanism: external, and the new child resumes it from the first unchecked step

cases.given: a project is withdrawn while its child is still running (restore-state)
cases.when: the child finishes and the next tick runs
cases.then: the in-flight run completes normally; no new launch for that project

cases.given: conductor.md has enabled: false or paused: true despite tick-source: launchd
cases.then: skip: conductor disabled/paused; nothing spawned

cases.given: a project directory with or without a conductor.md
cases.when: iterate-run nightly enroll / withdraw run, and the plist is rendered
cases.then: tick-source: launchd is written exactly once (file created with enabled: true when absent) and removed on withdraw with other keys intact; the plist is ProcessType Standard with StartInterval 600 and no LowPriorityIO

requirements.requirement: Status bar: orange = queued (locked and loaded), the project's next-plan letter is always shown dimmed at the end, and an alarm-clock icon marks a project enrolled in the nightly timer. An executing plan whose heartbeat is older than ITERATE_LIVE_SECS (or missing) renders dark green with ⚙️; a live one renders bold green with ⚡.

cases.given: a plan with phase: planned and status: queued in its key block
cases.then: its letter is orange (38;5;208 on a 256-colour terminal)

cases.given: a plan with phase: planned and no status
cases.then: its letter is yellow, unchanged

cases.given: a plan whose key block carries both status: blocked-on-operator and status: queued
cases.then: red wins

cases.given: a project with .claude/iterate/ but zero plans (only archive/)
cases.then: the ⚙️ segment is present with only the dim next-plan letter

cases.given: a project whose project_next_idx in plan-names.json is 6
cases.then: the trailing placeholder is a dim lowercase g, after every real plan letter

cases.given: a project not present in plan-names.json
cases.then: the placeholder is a dim a

cases.given: conductor.md has tick-source: launchd and nightly.json is not disabled
cases.then: the segment ends with ⏰

cases.given: conductor.md has tick-source: launchd and nightly.json has enabled: false
cases.then: the segment ends with ⏰ followed by dim off

cases.given: a project without tick-source: launchd
cases.then: no ⏰

cases.given: TERM=xterm with no COLORTERM
cases.then: the letter uses the 16-colour fallback (bright yellow 93), never a raw 256 escape

cases.given: current_dir is a subdirectory of a project whose plans are all archived
cases.then: the segment still renders (root walk accepts .claude/iterate, stops at .git)

cases.given: a plan with phase: executing and this project's heartbeat file younger than ITERATE_LIVE_SECS
cases.when: the statusline renders on a 256-colour terminal
cases.then: its letter is bold green (1;32) and the icon is ⚡

cases.given: a plan with phase: executing and the heartbeat file older than ITERATE_LIVE_SECS
cases.when: the statusline renders on a 256-colour terminal
cases.then: its letter is dark green (38;5;28) and the icon is ⚙️

cases.given: a plan with phase: executing and no heartbeat file for this project
cases.when: the statusline renders on a 256-colour terminal
cases.then: its letter is dark green (38;5;28) and the icon is ⚙️ — missing reads as stale

cases.given: a plan with phase: executing and a stale heartbeat
cases.when: the statusline renders with TERM=xterm and COLORTERM unset (ANSI-16 tier)
cases.then: its letter is plain green (32), the 16-colour fallback, and the icon is ⚙️

cases.given: a plan with phase: executing and the heartbeat aged exactly ITERATE_LIVE_SECS
cases.then: the plan still counts as live: bold green and ⚡ (boundary is inclusive)

cases.given: a stalled executing plan whose heartbeat is then refreshed by a hook
cases.then: its letter returns to bold green and the icon to ⚡ — stalled is a reading, not a latched state

requirements.requirement: The Go schedule evaluator matches /iterate-rules: deny beats allow, any allow makes default-deny, a window wraps midnight when start > end, a day label matches the day the window opened, and conductor-schedule can only narrow launch-schedule.

cases.given: allow mon-fri 22:00-06:00
cases.then: allowed

cases.given: allow mon-fri 22:00-06:00
cases.then: allowed (window opened Friday 22:00)

cases.given: allow mon-fri 22:00-06:00
cases.then: refused; next window Monday 22:00

cases.given: allow daily 22:00-06:00 and deny sat,sun
cases.then: refused: deny beats allow

cases.given: one allow rule exists
cases.then: refused: allow makes default-deny

cases.given: no launch-schedule and no conductor-schedule
cases.then: allowed, rule: none

cases.given: launch-schedule allows 22:00-06:00, conductor-schedule allows 00:00-23:59
cases.then: refused by launch-schedule: the conductor schedule cannot widen

cases.given: launch-schedule allows 22:00-06:00, conductor-schedule allows 23:00-02:00
cases.then: refused by conductor-schedule: it narrowed

cases.given: a malformed rule line
cases.then: the line is reported by name and treated as deny (fail closed), the rest still parse

requirements.requirement: /iterate-planner can stage a plan (status: queued) so the nightly tick or /iterate <name> can launch it; editing a staged plan unstages it; staging an executing plan is refused.

cases.given: a phase: planned plan
cases.then: status: queued is written in the key block and /ip list shows (queued)
cases.evidence: claude -p "/ip stage otter" in fixture g11 (5.11.0): status: queued written below phase; /ip list shows (current) (queued)

cases.given: a queued plan
cases.then: status: queued is removed; the plan is yellow again
cases.evidence: claude -p "/ip unstage otter" in fixture g11 (5.11.0): status line removed

cases.given: a phase: executing plan
cases.then: refused with a one-line reason; file untouched
cases.evidence: claude -p "/ip stage panda" (executing) in fixture g11 (5.11.0): refused in one line, file byte-identical

cases.given: a queued plan
cases.then: the step is added, status: queued is removed, and the reply says it was unstaged
cases.evidence: claude -p "/ip add to otter …" in fixture g11 (5.11.0): step 2 added, status removed, reply "unstaged — re-stage with /ip stage otter"

cases.given: a queued plan
cases.then: the plan launches now and status: queued is cleared on transition to executing
cases.evidence: claude -p "/iterate robin" in fixture g12 (5.11.0): status: queued cleared on transition, loop-mechanism external kept, 1/1 green, archived

cases.given: a queued plan and a no-arg /iterate tick with nothing executing
cases.then: the tick does not launch it (unattended launch belongs to the conductor), per the existing no-arg rules
cases.evidence: claude -p "/iterate" (no arg) in fixture g11b with one queued plan (5.11.0): printed the pointer, launched nothing, still on main

cases.given: a plan with status: queued in its key block
cases.when: iterate-run status and the dashboard render it
cases.then: status prints `plan <name> queued` and the card badge reads queued; executing and any status: blocked*/paused/unblocked still win

cases.given: a project with a position in the name registry
cases.then: both print the same letter and word, the registry is byte-identical, and a following name next hands out exactly that word

requirements.requirement: When the user says iterate, the executor works to completion: pause is a human verb, machine time (VM hours, slow tests, long builds) is never a reason to stop or ask for a go-ahead, the loop is cancelled only at a terminal ending, and a slow-tier case drifted by the plan's own work runs inside the plan while nobody is watching.

cases.given: an executing plan whose FFIV drift set contains a slow-tier case and nobody is at the keyboard
cases.then: it runs the case to completion (registry runs += 1), checks the step off, and neither pauses nor cancels its loop
cases.evidence: claude -p "/iterate seal" in fixture g14 (2026-10-05T05:20-05:24Z, 5.11.0): soak-1 run in-plan via iterate-run run --plan seal (125.3s), registry runs 2, plan all-green

cases.given: a step whose only cost is machine time (VM hours, a >2-minute test, a long build)
cases.when: the executor weighs whether to proceed
cases.then: it proceeds — the plan's Cost: line is the authority — and the transcript contains no 'go-ahead', 'pause the plan' or 'let me know when' text
cases.evidence: fixture g14 transcript daefaff3: 0 assistant-text matches for go-ahead|pause the plan|let me know when|before I run|say-so|^Ask:

cases.given: a plan file carrying status: paused
cases.then: a 'paused by operator' line from /iterate pause or /ic pause accompanies it — a pause with no human command behind it is a defect
cases.evidence: claude -p "/iterate-conductor run" in fixture /tmp/claude-503/fx/v13b (2026-10-05T04:09-04:14Z): status: paused with no operator line logged as "self-pause defect: heron", status cleared, resumed via /iterate heron with loop-mechanism: external, completed and archived

cases.given: an armed resumption loop or cron
cases.then: the same turn writes one of the four terminal endings (all-green, human-gate, blocked-on-operator after the ladder, giveup) or records a human pause/kill — never 'awaiting go-ahead'
cases.evidence: fixture g14 transcript: CronCreate once at launch, CronDelete 1cc25e0a once in the terminal all-green entry

cases.given: a plan with human-gate: N and every other validation green
cases.then: success-with-handoff fires exactly as before — the one designed stop is unchanged
cases.evidence: claude -p "/iterate gannet" in fixture g14b (5.11.0): status: awaiting-human-gate set, loop cancelled and field cleared, gate question asked, ⚠ branch-not-merged line

cases.given: /testmaster run invoked from inside an executing plan
cases.when: the selection names a drifted slow case by id
cases.then: it runs without a confirmation prompt; bare 'all' during the same plan still downgrades to fast+standard with the one-line note
cases.evidence: claude -p "/testmaster run soak-1" in fixture v15 (plan executing): ran 125s without confirmation; "/testmaster run all" downgraded to fast+standard with the note

cases.given: the conductor sweeps and finds a plan with status: paused and no operator pause line
cases.then: it logs 'self-pause defect', clears the status, and resumes the plan
cases.evidence: claude -p "/iterate-conductor run" in fixture /tmp/claude-503/fx/v13b (2026-10-05T04:09-04:14Z): status: paused with no operator line logged as "self-pause defect: heron", status cleared, resumed via /iterate heron with loop-mechanism: external, completed and archived

requirements.requirement: Every box the tutorial runtime draws (the run.sh menu, tut_title, tut_done) is closed on all four sides and sized to its widest row. The menu shows a bucket's time as one line: ~45 min running (10 hands-on) when it declares TUTORIAL-WALLCLOCK, 10 min otherwise. Durations are dim, and the colour roles are the skill's standard.

cases.given: the menu, a tut_title box and a tut_done box rendered on a pty at 60, 80 and 132 columns
cases.when: the frames are read with ANSI stripped
cases.then: every line of each box has the same width and ends in its right border

cases.given: a row wider than the terminal (a long tut_title subtitle, a long menu row)
cases.when: the box renders at 60, 80 and 132 columns
cases.then: the row wraps inside the frame and no line is wider than the terminal

cases.given: a bucket declaring TUTORIAL-MINUTES: 10 and TUTORIAL-WALLCLOCK: 45
cases.then: its duration reads ~45 min running (10 hands-on)

cases.given: a bucket declaring only TUTORIAL-MINUTES: 4 beside the box-3 bucket
cases.then: its duration reads 4 min and starts in the same column as box-3's

cases.given: NO_COLOR=1, TERM=dumb, or a piped stdout
cases.when: the menu or a bucket renders
cases.then: the output holds no escape sequence and every frame is closed

cases.given: LANG=C LC_ALL=C
cases.then: the frame is drawn in + - | and is closed

cases.given: a tutorial directory with no buckets
cases.then: a closed frame shows the (no tutorials yet …) placeholder row

requirements.requirement: tern must never have parked on "extend symapi or withdraw --no-browser": when a feature needs an API broadly expanded, iterate expands it, chases the regressions (revalidating old code is fine), implements the feature and moves forward without human interaction.

cases.given: skills/iterate/SKILL.md
cases.then: rule 33 exists, names contract expansion, answers extend-or-withdraw with extend, and cites tern

cases.given: /iterate's On-stuck and landing-test Fails paragraphs
cases.then: the operator-only list is closed to a secret, physical access and an external party with no decision on it, and a clause-3/4 failure is work

cases.given: the conductor's escalation ladder
cases.then: a parity row ends in continue and no 'needs a human decision' row exists

cases.given: the triage state table
cases.then: exactly one Executor-defect row exists, cleared with fix problem N and status: unblocked

cases.given: the 13 iterate family members
cases.when: skillctl family iterate runs and each installed copy is compared with its source
cases.then: every member carries the family version and every installed copy matches
